ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Mary Seacole — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Four-week review: blood pressure, sodium and potassium on chlorthalidone, echocardiogram, statin decision, knee exercise program and cane

text.paragraph: Four-week review on two blood pressure medicines. [S]

Mary Seacole returns four weeks after starting amlodipine and chlorthalidone. Her headaches stopped in the second week. Her home readings average 134/80. She has had no dizziness on standing and no ankle swelling. She began physical therapy three weeks ago, does her exercises most days and uses the cane the therapist fitted, in her right hand. The occupational therapist visited and a rail is being fitted on the stairs to her rooms. She has met the social prescribing link worker, who found a tai chi class near her home. Her knees hurt less. She wants to talk about the cholesterol tablet. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1877-04-13; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 138/82 seated, 134/80 standing at three minutes, pulse 76; weight 77.6 kg
Regular rhythm; no murmur; no edema
No knee effusion; Timed Up and Go 14 seconds with the cane

Headaches on waking for three weeks and blood pressure 184/102 mmHg at the visit (average of two seated readings with a large cuff); no chest pain, breathlessness, visual loss, confusion or weakness; fundi with arteriolar narrowing but no hemorrhages or papilledema; no hypertensive emergency; hypertension not yet confirmed
S — Synthetic presenting problem; resolved into stage 2 hypertension when a week of home readings confirmed it. Not a claim about her real health.

Stage 2 hypertension confirmed by home readings (seven-day average 168/96 mmHg), with left ventricular hypertrophy by ECG voltage; no albuminuria; 10-year cardiovascular risk about 14%; treated to reduce the risk of stroke, heart failure and kidney disease

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit. It is linked to the recorded apoplexy before her death only as the reason for the stroke-prevention teaching; the record does not claim that she had hypertension.

Bilateral primary knee osteoarthritis, worse on the left: pain on stairs and on rising from a chair, morning stiffness under 30 minutes, crepitus and bony enlargement without warmth; clinical diagnosis without imaging
S — Synthetic modern problem; not a claim about her real health.
Fall risk: one fall in the past year, a trip on the outside steps without injury; afraid of falling and going out less; STEADI screen positive; Timed Up and Go 15 seconds
Obesity, class 1 (BMI 31.6); she calls herself stout and wants to lose some weight for her knees
S — Synthetic modern problem; her self-description as stout is documented, her weight is not.

value.displayName: Elevated blood-pressure reading, without diagnosis of hypertension

list.item:
Stage 2 hypertension (I10). Much improved: 138/82 in the clinic and 134/80 at home, not yet below 130/80. Sodium 136 and potassium 3.7 mmol/L, at the low end of normal on chlorthalidone; creatinine 0.95 mg/dL. Echocardiogram: ejection fraction 64% with mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, no heart failure. With a 10-year risk of about 14% and LDL 146 mg/dL, a moderate-intensity statin lowers her risk of stroke and heart attack; she chose to start it. [S]
Continue amlodipine 5 mg and chlorthalidone 12.5 mg; reassess at three months.
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily; lipid panel in four to twelve weeks.
Remember the sick-day rule for chlorthalidone.

Knee osteoarthritis (M17.0). Pain 5 out of 10; KOOS JR 56.6, up from 52.5. [S]
Continue exercise therapy; start tai chi when the physical therapy course ends.

Follow-up: Three-month review in nine weeks. Stop chlorthalidone and call if she cannot eat or drink normally. Next scheduled visit 1877-06-15: three-month review after chlorthalidone was stopped: blood pressure above target, losartan added; lipids on atorvastatin; knee and falls. [S]
